newsitem.title: UK: Boeing to seek close links with BAe - paper.
newsitem.headline: Boeing to seek close links with BAe - paper.

text.p: U.S. aircraft maker Boeing Co wants to increase its ties with British Aerospace Plc (Bae) and other international aerospace companies, according to a report in the Financial Times.
In an interview with the paper, Boeing chairman Philip Condit said he wanted Boeing to grow internationally so it was no longer seen as an American group.
"I believe we are moving towards an era of global markets and global companies," he told the paper. "I think it is advantageous that your workforce, your executive corps, reflect that."
The FT said Condit saw Bae as a possible partner on the planned U.S. Joint Strike Fighter.
The British firm unsuccessfully bid for the fighter contract last year in a consortium including McDonnell Douglas, subsequently bid for by Boeing, and Northrop Grumman Corp.
No one at Bae was immediately available for comment on the interview.

The FT pointed out that Bae was already a partner of McDonnell on the Harrier jump jet while Boeing was a subcontractor to Bae to provide replacements for the UK's fleet of Nimrod maritime patrol aircraft.
